The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Strategy CFO Andrew Kang resigns as company posts record operating profit. Andrew Kang’s departure comes as Strategy reports $21 billion in quarterly operating income and bitcoin holdings of 848,517 BTC. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Binance finds more breaches in $6.3 billion hack; AI spending fears hit tech. A $6.3 billion Binance hack adds to crypto jitters, while weak earnings outlooks and mounting concerns over AI spending push QQQ down more than 2%. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Binance hacker dumps a little-known 2017 token and it crashes 90%. The hacker dumped FUN and other smaller tokens into markets too small to absorb large selling, leading to price crashes. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin, ether and XRP selloff wipes out $1.5 billion in leveraged crypto bets. Bets on rising prices accounted for nearly 84% of forced closures, with Binance handling almost half the total. A rebound has since started catching short sellers. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

XRP Ledger developers tighten the rules for who can hold 'restricted' tokens. A set of fixes would tighten who can hold permissioned tokens on the network. The XRP Ledger Foundation says no users were affected. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Binance hack bites India's largest crypto exchange as it curbs futures trading. CoinDCX has restricted new futures positions after Binance’s security incident disrupted a key liquidity provider. Deposits, withdrawals and customer funds remain unaffected, the exchange said. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,316 with a -3.40% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,220.59 with a -4.09% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto Regulation in 2026: What Changed and What’s Ahead
items.description:
Regulatory trends

Stablecoin legislation

In July 2025, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act legislation into law, requiring stablecoins to be backed 1-to-1 by the US dollar or other low-risk assets. The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

SEC and CFTC crypto clarity [...] Hong Kong has introduced a dedicated stablecoin issuer licensing regime under the HKMA and FSTB. It proposes high-quality reserve-asset backing, segregation and custody requirements, independent audits, clear redemption rights, and governance standards. Algorithmic stablecoins and unbacked arrangements will face restrictions.

ETF & tokenized-asset guidelines [...] Stablecoin payment rules in the UK are still in development and have not yet come into force. The government has outlined a future framework in which stablecoins used for payments would be subject to requirements on backing, redemption, and issuer governance, with payment-system regulators gaining expanded supervisory powers over systemic arrangements. # Congress Enacts Comprehensive Stablecoin Legislation: Key Provisions and Implications of the GENIUS Act

The first federal framework for U.S. dollar stablecoins was signed into law last week, spelling out who can issue stablecoins and setting rigorous reserve and operational requirements. The law establishes three paths to become a stablecoin issuer—as a bank subsidiary, with a federal license, or with a state license.
